Class SudokuGame

java.lang.Object
com.examplez.demo.models.SudokuGame
All Implemented Interfaces:
SudokuInitializable
public class SudokuGame extends Object implements SudokuInitializable
Game-logic model for a 6×6 Sudoku puzzle.

Responsibilities of this class:

  • Generate a fully solved, randomized 6×6 board using a recursive backtracking algorithm.
  • Select a distributed set of initial cells to reveal as starting clues.
  • Validate player real-time entries against standard Sudoku constraints (unique values per row, column, and 2×3 sub-block).
  • Evaluate board completion based on the confirmed-cell state mask.
  • Provide utility and coordinate-lookup methods consumed by the presentation layer.

The grid uses a standard 6×6 Sudoku layout divided into six 2-row × 3-column sub-blocks.

Version:
1.1
Author:
jeronimo rojas imbachi, Luis Felipe Velasco

  • Constructor Details

    • SudokuGame

      public SudokuGame()
      Constructs a new SudokuGame instance with an empty, unsolved grid.

      Allocates two 6×6 nested ArrayList structures: matrixSudokuSolve, pre-filled with "0" to represent empty cells, and confirmedCells, pre-filled with false to mark every cell as unconfirmed.

  • Method Details

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Generates a complete, structurally valid, and randomized Sudoku board, then selects the initial clues to expose to the player.

      Delegates board generation to the recursive backtracking routine solve(int, int) starting at position (0, 0). After solve returns, matrixSudokuSolve is guaranteed to hold a fully filled legal solution. chooseCluesToShow() is then called to populate confirmedCells with the starting hints.

      Specified by:
      initialize in interface SudokuInitializable

    • getConfirmedCells

      public ArrayList<ArrayList<Boolean>> getConfirmedCells()
      Returns the full 6×6 confirmed-cells mask for the current game session.

      Each element is true when the corresponding cell holds a finalized or initially revealed value, and false while the cell is still editable or empty.

      Returns:
      the internal ArrayList of boolean rows representing the confirmed state of every board position

    • setConfirmedStateOfCell

      public void setConfirmedStateOfCell(int column, int row, boolean confirmedState)
      Updates the confirmed state of a single cell in the tracking mask.

      Setting a cell to true marks it as finalized (correctly placed or revealed as a clue). Setting it to false marks it as unresolved or conflicting.

      Parameters:
      column - zero-based column index of the target cell
      row - zero-based row index of the target cell
      confirmedState - true to finalize the cell; false to revert it to an unresolved state

    • getConfirmedStateOfCell

      public boolean getConfirmedStateOfCell(int column, int row)

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      true if the cell is finalized or was revealed as a clue; false if it is still editable or unresolved

    • getCoordinatesRepeatedInvalidCells

      public List<List<Integer>> getCoordinatesRepeatedInvalidCells(String value, int column, int row, ArrayList<ArrayList<String>> cells)
      Identifies cells that conflict with a newly placed value and marks them as unconfirmed.

      Checks the same row, column, and 2×3 sub-block for occurrences of value at positions other than the origin (row, column). For each conflicting cell found, its confirmed state is set to false so the UI can highlight it as invalid.

      Parameters:
      value - the digit string ("1"–"6") just placed
      column - zero-based column index of the newly placed value
      row - zero-based row index of the newly placed value
      cells - the current 6×6 string value matrix of the board
      Returns:
      a list of [row, col] coordinate pairs for every cell that now conflicts with the placed digit; empty if no conflicts exist

    • getRepeatedValidCells

      public List<List<Integer>> getRepeatedValidCells(String value, int column, int row, ArrayList<ArrayList<String>> cells)
      Identifies previously conflicting cells that become valid after a value is removed from the board, and marks them as confirmed.

      When a player deletes an entry, neighbours sharing the same row, column, or sub-block may no longer have a conflict. This method re-evaluates those neighbours: if a neighbour's current value now satisfies all Sudoku constraints and is not already confirmed, its confirmed state is updated to true.

      Parameters:
      value - the digit string ("1"–"6") just removed
      column - zero-based column index of the removed value
      row - zero-based row index of the removed value
      cells - the current 6×6 string value matrix of the board (the cell at [row][column] should already reflect the deletion, i.e. contain "0")
      Returns:
      a list of [row, col] coordinate pairs for every neighbour cell that transitioned to a valid state; empty if none changed

    • giveClue

      public List<Integer> giveClue(ArrayList<ArrayList<String>> cells)
      Returns the coordinates of the first empty cell on the board in row-major order, to be used as the next clue position.

      Scans the board left-to-right, top-to-bottom and returns the [row, col] indices of the first cell whose value equals "0".

      Parameters:
      cells - the current 6×6 string value matrix of the board, where "0" represents an unfilled cell
      Returns:
      a two-element list [row, col] identifying the first empty cell; an empty list if every cell is already filled

    • isPossibleGiveClue

      public boolean isPossibleGiveClue(ArrayList<ArrayList<String>> cells)
      Determines whether another clue may be dispensed to the player.

      Two conditions independently block further clues:

      • 35 or more cells are already confirmed, forcing the player to place the last value manually.
      • All 36 cells are filled (no empty cell exists to reveal).
      Parameters:
      cells - the current 6×6 string value matrix of the board
      Returns:
      true if a clue can still be given; false if either blocking condition is met

    • getValue

      public String getValue(int row, int col)
      Returns the solution value at the given board position.

      Since initialize() always produces a fully solved board before this method is called, the returned value is always a digit string ("1"–"6") and never "0".

      Parameters:
      row - zero-based row index
      col - zero-based column index
      Returns:
      the digit string stored in the solution matrix at (row, col)

    • printBoard

      public void printBoard()
      Prints the complete solution board (matrixSudokuSolve) to standard output.

      A horizontal divider is printed before every third row and a vertical pipe (|) before every third column to visually separate the 2×3 sub-blocks.

    • printBoardBool

      public void printBoardBool()
      Prints the confirmedCells boolean mask to standard output.

      Uses the same visual layout as printBoard() (horizontal dividers and pipe separators aligned with sub-block boundaries) to make it easy to compare the confirmed-cell state against the solution board during debugging.
